senses.title: Extreme tiredness of body or mind
senses.definition: the state of being so tired that you can hardly move, think, or speak
senses.definitionCN: 累到几乎无法行动、思考或说话的状态
senses.example: Three nights without sleep left him in a state of total exhaustion.
senses.exampleCN: 三个晚上没睡，他整个人处于彻底的精疲力竭之中。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to drain a vessel dry, so a person is pictured as a container with nothing left inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是把容器抽干，于是人被想象成一只见底的容器，力气一滴不剩。

senses.title: The using up of a supply
senses.definition: the act or result of using all of a supply until none of it remains
senses.definitionCN: 把某样储备全部用掉、直到一点不剩的行为或结果
senses.example: The exhaustion of the coal reserves forced the town to look for other work.
senses.exampleCN: 煤炭储备的枯竭迫使这个镇子去寻找别的生计。
senses.why: Once the empty vessel is applied to coal, oil, or money, the word names the state of the store rather than of the body.
senses.whyCN: 把「空容器」从人身上挪到煤、石油或金钱上，这个词就指仓库空了，而不是人累了。

senses.title: The drawing out of air or liquid
senses.definition: the removal of air, gas, or liquid from a closed space
senses.definitionCN: 把空气、气体或液体从一个封闭空间里抽走
senses.example: The exhaustion of air from the glass tube takes only a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 把玻璃管里的空气抽空只需要几秒钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical layer, still used for pumps and vacuum work, and it is the picture all the other senses grew from.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最具体的一层，至今仍用于泵与真空作业，也是其余各义项生长出来的那幅画。

senses.title: A collapse of bodily function
senses.definition: a medical condition in which the body or one of its organs can no longer work properly
senses.definitionCN: 身体或某个器官无法正常运转的医学状态
senses.example: He was treated for heat exhaustion after the long march.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军之后，他因热衰竭接受了治疗。
senses.why: Doctors borrowed the word for the moment when the body has spent its reserves and the system starts to fail, as in heat exhaustion.
senses.whyCN: 医生借用这个词，指身体把储备花光、系统开始失灵的那一刻，热衰竭就是典型例子。

senses.title: The using up of every available step
senses.definition: the state of having tried every possible remedy, argument, or option
senses.definitionCN: 已经把一切可用的救济、理由或选择都试遍的状态
senses.example: The claim was dismissed because there was no proof of exhaustion of local remedies.
senses.exampleCN: 由于没有证据表明已用尽当地救济，该请求被驳回。
senses.why: In law and in logic the container becomes a set of options, and exhaustion means that the set is now empty.
senses.whyCN: 在法律和逻辑里，容器变成了「一组选项」，耗尽就意味着这组选项已经被取空。

intro.en: Exhaustion goes back to Latin exhaurire, to draw water out of a vessel until it is dry.
intro.cn: exhaustion 可上溯到拉丁语 exhaurire，意为把水从容器里舀出来、直到见底。

items.en: Haurire means to draw water or to drain a container.
items.cn: haurire 意为舀水，或把容器里的东西排干。

items.en: The prefix ex- adds the direction out, giving exhaurire, to draw out or drain dry.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加上「向外」的方向，构成 exhaurire，意为抽出、排干。

items.en: The participle exhaustus describes something already drained.
items.cn: 分词 exhaustus 描述已经被抽空的东西。

items.en: Exhaustio names the act of draining out and passes into medieval learned Latin.
items.cn: exhaustio 把「抽干」这一动作变成名词，并进入中世纪的学术拉丁语。

items.en: English borrows exhaustion to name the state of a person or a fund that has been drained.
items.cn: 英语借入 exhaustion，用来指人或资金被抽干之后的状态。

items.en: The word spreads to medicine and to law, giving heat exhaustion and the exhaustion of remedies.
items.cn: 这个词延伸到医学与法律，产生热衰竭与用尽救济等说法。

note.en: Exhaustion sits in the family of exhaust, exhausted, and inexhaustible, and near the ordinary words for being worn out.
note.cn: exhaustion 与 exhaust、exhausted、inexhaustible 同属一族，也与表示「累垮」的普通词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 使精疲力竭；把某物用光

entries.definitionCN: 疲乏；劳累，多指努力或生病之后的疲倦

entries.definition: total loss of energy caused by long term stress at work
entries.definitionCN: 长期工作压力造成的彻底耗竭

entries.definition: a large reduction in the amount of something available
entries.definitionCN: 储备或数量的大幅减少

normalIntro.en: Keep the picture of a vessel turned upside down: exhaustion is what remains when nothing is left inside.
normalIntro.cn: 记住那只被倒过来的容器：exhaustion 就是里面什么都不剩时的状态。

normal.en: Physical exhaustion arrives after hours of hard work.
normal.cn: 体力上的精疲力竭总在数小时苦干之后到来。

normal.en: Heat exhaustion is a real danger in a hot workshop.
normal.cn: 在炎热的车间里，热衰竭是实实在在的危险。

normal.en: The exhaustion of fossil fuels is a slow process.
normal.cn: 化石燃料的枯竭是一个缓慢的过程。

normal.en: Add -ed and you get exhausted, the feeling in the body; add -ing and you get exhausting, the quality of the task.
normal.cn: 加上 -ed 得到 exhausted，是身体里的感觉；加上 -ing 得到 exhausting，是那件事的性质。

normal.en: Compare fatigue: fatigue is tiredness you can still push through, exhaustion is the point where you stop.
normal.cn: 对比 fatigue：fatigue 是还能撑住的疲倦，exhaustion 是撑不住的那一刻。

abstract.en: Picture a phone at one percent, the screen dimming as you speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一部只剩百分之一的手机，你说话时屏幕正在变暗。

abstract.en: Imagine a jar of coins tipped over, one last coin rolling across the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐硬币被倒过来，最后一枚硬币滚过桌面。

abstract.en: Think of a straw in a glass pulling up the very last of the water with a loud slurp.
abstract.cn: 想象一根吸管把杯底最后一点水吸上来，发出很大的响声。

examples.en: After two night shifts she was close to collapse from exhaustion.
examples.cn: 两个夜班之后，她累得几乎要倒下。

examples.en: The exhaustion of the city water supply alarmed the engineers.
examples.cn: 城市供水的枯竭让工程师们警觉起来。

examples.en: He slept for twelve hours and still felt the exhaustion in his legs.
examples.cn: 他睡了十二个小时，双腿仍旧酸软无力。

dict_mnemonic.text: exhaustion 中间的 haust 读起来像「耗死他」：力气被一点一点耗光，人就瘫在那里；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ haurire（舀水、排干）→ exhaurire（抽空、排尽）→ 分词 exhaustus → 晚期拉丁语 exhaustio → 英语 exhaustion，核心义「把里面的东西抽到一滴不剩」。

sensesIntro.en: A vessel drained dry gives the physical act, then the empty supply, then the emptied body, then medical failure, and finally a set of options with nothing left to try.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只被抽干的容器先给出具体动作，再给出见底的储备，接着是空掉的身体、医学上的衰竭，最后是一组再也无计可施的选项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup held upside down, not one drop left inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被倒扣的杯子，里面一滴不剩。

branches.en: Pumping air or water out of a closed space is the literal core.
branches.cn: 把空气或水从封闭空间里抽走，是这个词最字面的核心。

branches.en: A drained store of coal or money is the same vessel seen as a resource.
branches.cn: 被抽空的煤或钱，是同一只容器被看作资源的样子。

branches.en: A person with no strength left is the vessel read as a body.
branches.cn: 一个人力气全无，就是这只容器被读成了身体。

branches.en: When the body stops working altogether, the everyday tiredness becomes a medical condition.
branches.cn: 当身体彻底停摆，日常的疲倦就变成了医学上的衰竭。

branches.en: In law the vessel holds remedies, and exhaustion means the last one has been used.
branches.cn: 在法律里，容器装的是救济手段，耗尽意味着最后一条也已被用掉。

intro.en: Exhaustion is built from the Latin verb exhaurire plus the noun ending -ion, with exhaust, exhausted, and inexhaustible around it.
intro.cn: exhaustion 由拉丁语动词 exhaurire 加名词词尾 -ion 构成，周围还有 exhaust、exhausted 与 inexhaustible。

latinIntro.en: Latin haurire means to draw water, and the prefix ex- turns it into drawing water out until the vessel is dry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haurire 意为舀水，前缀 ex- 把它变成「把水舀出去、直到容器见底」。

items.example: The prefix ex- gives the movement an outward direction.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 给这个动作一个向外的方向。

items.example: Haurire names lifting water out of a well.
items.exampleCN: haurire 指把水从井里提上来。

items.meaning: to draw out, to drain dry
items.example: Exhaurire joins the prefix to the verb.
items.exampleCN: exhaurire 把前缀与动词合在一起。
exhaustus 描述那只空了的容器。

items.example: Exhaustio turns the action into a thing that can be named.
items.exampleCN: exhaustio 把这个动作变成可以被命名的东西。

items.meaningCN: 动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion carries exhaustio into English.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把 exhaustio 带进英语。

items.example: Exhaustion is the noun in use today.
items.exampleCN: exhaustion 是今天使用的名词。

items.meaning: to tire out, to use up
items.example: Exhaust is the shorter verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: exhaust 是名词背后那个更短的动词。

items.example: Exhausted describes the person who has nothing left.
items.exampleCN: exhausted 描述那个什么都不剩的人。

items.example: The prefix in- reverses the idea of being drained.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把「被抽干」这个意思反过来。

definition_zh: 详尽的；彻底的；穷举的
definition_en: covering every part or possibility of something, so that nothing is left out
core_image: 一张网眼细密的网，任何一条小鱼都漏不过去
scene: 审阅报告的编辑把每一页脚注都核了一遍，连附录也不放过。The editor gave the report an exhaustive check, down to the last footnote.
sceneCN: 这里 exhaustive 是「详尽的」（第 1 个义项：内容一项不缺）；句意：编辑对报告做了详尽核查，连最后一条脚注都没放过。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly，义为「详尽地；彻底地」
形容词加 -ness，义为「详尽；无遗漏」
形容词所由来的动词，义为「抽干；耗尽」
同族名词，义为「精疲力竭；耗尽」

senses.title: Covering every part of a subject
senses.definition: including every part or detail of a subject, so that nothing is left out
senses.definitionCN: 把某个主题的每个部分或细节都包含进来，一项也不遗漏
senses.example: The book gives an exhaustive account of the history of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书详尽地记述了这座小镇的历史。
senses.why: The Latin participle meant drained dry, and an account that drains its subject leaves no detail behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词本义是「被抽干的」，而一份把题目抽干的记述，不会剩下任何细节。

senses.title: Leaving nothing untried
senses.definition: done with such care and effort that every possibility has been tested
senses.definitionCN: 做得足够仔细、足够用力，以至于每一种可能都被试过
senses.example: The police made an exhaustive search of the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 警方对那所空房子做了彻底搜查。
senses.why: Here the vessel is a set of possibilities, and a careful worker keeps going until the set is empty.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是一组可能性，认真的人会一直查到这组可能性被取空为止。

senses.title: Trying every case in turn
senses.definition: in computing and logic, describing a method that tests every possible case one by one
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机与逻辑领域，指把每一种可能情况逐一检验的方法
senses.example: An exhaustive search of all the keys finally broke the code.
senses.exampleCN: 对所有密钥的穷举搜索最终破解了密码。
senses.why: Technical use keeps the literal sense: no member of the set is skipped, so the count is complete.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法保留了字面义：集合里没有一个成员被跳过，所以统计才算完整。

senses.title: Tending to tire someone out
senses.definition: causing extreme tiredness, an older sense now mostly carried by exhausting
senses.definitionCN: 使人极度疲惫；这一旧义如今大多由 exhausting 承担
senses.example: The old diary speaks of an exhaustive day in the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧日记写到田里令人筋疲力尽的一天。
senses.why: The suffix first meant having the power to drain, so the adjective could name the cause as well as the completeness of a survey.
senses.whyCN: 这个词尾最初表示「有抽干之力」，所以形容词既能指致人疲惫的原因，也能指调查的完整。

intro.en: Exhaustive is the Latin participle exhaustus plus the suffix -ive, literally having the power to drain.
intro.cn: exhaustive 是拉丁语分词 exhaustus 加后缀 -ive，字面意思是「具有抽干之力的」。

items.en: Haurire means to draw water from a well or a jar.
items.cn: haurire 意为从井里或罐子里舀水。

items.en: Exhaurire adds ex-, out, and means to drain a vessel until it is dry.
items.cn: exhaurire 加上表示「向外」的 ex-，意为把容器抽到见底。

items.en: The participle exhaustus supplies the stem used by English.
items.cn: 分词 exhaustus 提供了英语所使用的那截词干。

items.en: English adds -ive and first uses exhaustive for things that drain strength.
items.cn: 英语加上 -ive，最初用 exhaustive 形容「会抽干力气」的事物。

items.en: The sense shifts from causing exhaustion to leaving nothing out, as a full account drains its subject.
items.cn: 词义从「致人疲惫」转向「无所遗漏」：一份完整的记述会把题目本身抽干。

items.en: Logic and computing give the word its technical life in exhaustive search and exhaustive proof.
items.cn: 逻辑学与计算机给它技术生命，出现了穷举搜索与穷举证明的说法。

note.en: Exhaustive shares its stem with exhaust and exhaustion, and stands beside the ordinary words for being complete.
note.cn: exhaustive 与 exhaust、exhaustion 共用词干，并与表示「完整」的普通词并列。

entries.definition: to drain someone of strength or to use something up
entries.definitionCN: 耗尽某人的力气；把某物用光

entries.definition: the state of being completely tired or used up
entries.definitionCN: 精疲力竭或耗尽的状态

entries.definition: too abundant to be used up
careful and complete in every detail
including everything that is relevant
entries.definitionCN: 包含一切相关内容的；综合的

entries.definition: giving many small facts and features

normalIntro.en: Think of a net whose holes are too small for anything to slip through: exhaustive means no gap is left.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一张网眼极小的网，什么都漏不过去：exhaustive 就是不留缝隙。

normal.en: An exhaustive list names every item, not just the main ones.
normal.cn: 一份详尽的清单会把每一项都列出来，而不只是主要的几项。

normal.en: An exhaustive search checks every room, corner, and drawer.
normal.cn: 一次彻底的搜查会检查每一间屋、每一个角落、每一个抽屉。

normal.en: The adverb is exhaustively, as in the question was exhaustively studied.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 exhaustively，例如这个问题被彻底研究过。

normal.en: Keep exhaustive apart from exhausting: a long report can be exhausting, but only a complete one is exhaustive.
normal.cn: 把 exhaustive 与 exhausting 分开：冗长的报告让人 exhausting，但只有完整的报告才 exhaustive。

normal.en: Compare exhaustive with comprehensive: comprehensive means wide coverage, exhaustive means no item is missing.
normal.cn: 对比 comprehensive 与 exhaustive：前者指覆盖面广，后者指一项不缺。

abstract.en: Picture a net pulled through a pond, and not a single fish slips out.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网拖过池塘，没有一条鱼漏出去。

abstract.en: Imagine turning over every stone in a yard, one after another, until the ground shows bare soil.
abstract.cn: 想象把院子里每一块石头都翻过来，一个接一个，直到地上只剩裸土。

abstract.en: Think of a ring of keys tried on a lock, one key after another, until the last one turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙一把接一把地试上锁孔，直到最后一把转动。

examples.en: The report is not exhaustive, but it covers the main causes of the failure.
examples.cn: 这份报告并不详尽，但涵盖了失败的主要原因。

examples.en: The police carried out an exhaustive search of the building.
examples.cn: 警方对这栋楼进行了彻底搜查。

examples.en: Her list of the birds in the valley was exhaustive.
examples.cn: 她列出的山谷鸟类清单十分详尽。

dict_mnemonic.text: exhaust 读起来像「耗死他」，末尾的 -ive 轻轻一带：把每个角落都耗上一遍、一个不漏，才叫详尽；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exhaurire（抽干）的分词 exhaustus + 词尾 -ive（有……性质的）→ exhaustive，本义「有抽干之力的」，后转指「把一个题目抽到一滴不剩」，即详尽无遗。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a force that drains, then names a complete account, then a process that tests every option, and keeps an older medical sense of tiring.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词最初指「会抽干」的力量，接着指完整的记述、把所有可能都试遍的过程，并保留一层古老的「使人疲惫」之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine mesh that lets nothing through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张细密的网，什么都漏不过去。

branches.en: A complete account of a subject is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对一个题目的完整记述，是最日常的义项。

branches.en: A process that tests every possibility is the effort sense.
branches.cn: 把每一种可能都试过的过程，是讲「用力到底」的义项。

branches.en: Machine logic narrows the same idea into a formal method.
branches.cn: 机器逻辑把同一个想法收紧成一种形式方法。

branches.en: The oldest layer still says that the thing itself drains you.
branches.cn: 最古老的那一层仍然表示「这东西本身会把你抽干」。

branches.en: A complete list and a thorough search both refuse to leave a single item behind.
branches.cn: 完整的清单与彻底的搜查都不肯留下任何一项。

intro.en: Exhaustive is the stem exhaust plus the suffix -ive, which marks a tendency or a quality, and the same suffix builds active, decisive, and protective.
intro.cn: exhaustive 是词干 exhaust 加后缀 -ive 构成，-ive 表示倾向或性质，同样的词尾还构成 active、decisive 与 protective。

latinIntro.en: Latin -ivus meant having the nature of, and it entered English through French as -ive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -ivus 意为「具有……性质的」，经法语进入英语成为 -ive。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks the outward pull of the water.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标出水流向外被拉走。

items.example: Haurire supplies the central image of the family.
items.exampleCN: haurire 提供这个词族的核心意象。

items.example: Exhaurire is the verb behind the whole group.
items.exampleCN: exhaurire 是整组词背后的那个动词。
exhaustus 给英语提供了词干。

items.meaning: having the nature of, tending to
items.meaningCN: 有……性质的；倾向于……的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ive turns a verb stem into a quality word.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把动词词干变成表示性质形容词。

items.example: Exhaustive describes the quality of a survey.
items.exampleCN: exhaustive 描述一份调查的性质。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: The suffix -ness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 把这种性质变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion builds exhaustion from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 用同一词干构成 exhaustion。

items.example: Exhaustion keeps the draining image as a noun.
items.exampleCN: exhaustion 以名词形式保留「被抽干」的意象。

definition_zh: 展出；陈列；表现出；展品
definition_en: to show something in public, to show a quality or symptom, or an object on display
core_image: 玻璃柜里的一件展品
scene: 博物馆展出了几件唐代陶器。The museum exhibited several Tang pottery pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 exhibit 是「展出、陈列」（第 1 个义项）；句意：博物馆展出了几件唐代陶器。

senses.title: Show in public
senses.definition: to show something in a public place for people to see
senses.definitionCN: 在公共场所陈列某物供人观看
senses.example: The gallery exhibits local paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出本地画作。
senses.why: The object is held out for the public eye.
senses.whyCN: 物品被举到公众眼前。

senses.title: Show a sign
senses.definition: to show a feeling, quality, or symptom
senses.definitionCN: 表现出某种情感、特质或症状
senses.example: The patient exhibited no signs of fever.
senses.exampleCN: 病人没有表现出发烧的迹象。
senses.why: An inner state is held out where others can see it.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态被展示出来让人看见。

senses.title: Displayed object
senses.definition: an object shown in a museum or public show
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆或公开展览中陈列的物品
senses.example: The gold mask is the finest exhibit here.
senses.exampleCN: 这件金面具是这里最精美的展品。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that is held out.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被展示出来的那件东西。

intro.en: Exhibit comes from Latin exhibere, to hold out.
intro.cn: exhibit 源自拉丁语 exhibere，意为向外持有、呈出。

items.en: Habere means to have or hold.
items.cn: habere 意为拥有、持有。

items.en: Exhibere joins ex-, out, with habere, to hold.
items.cn: exhibere 由 ex-（出）与 habere（持有）组成。

items.en: Exhibere means to present or display.
items.cn: exhibere 意为呈出、展示。

items.en: English exhibit keeps the public display sense.
items.cn: 英语 exhibit 保留公开展示的含义。

items.en: Exhibit also becomes a noun for a displayed object.
items.cn: exhibit 又变成名词，指陈列的物件。

note.en: Exhibit holds an object out; inhibit holds a person back.
note.cn: exhibit 把东西举出来，inhibit 则把人拦住。

entries.definition: a public show of objects
a person or firm that shows goods
to stop or slow something
to put something where it can be seen
to let something be seen
to offer something for viewing

normalIntro.en: Exhibit holds an object or a sign out for others.
normalIntro.cn: exhibit 把物品或迹象举出来给人看。

normal.en: The museum exhibits ancient tools.
normal.cn: 博物馆展出古代工具。

normal.en: The patient exhibited a mild cough.
normal.cn: 病人表现出轻微咳嗽。

normal.en: The gold mask is a famous exhibit.
normal.cn: 金面具是一件著名展品。

normal.en: Local artists exhibit at the hall each spring.
normal.cn: 本地艺术家每年春天在大厅展出。

normal.en: The painting is on exhibit until June.
normal.cn: 这幅画展出到六月。

abstract.en: Picture an object under a glass case.
abstract.cn: 想象一件放在玻璃柜里的物品。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand holding a card up to a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把卡片举向人群。

abstract.en: Think of a face that shows a hidden mood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张显露内心情绪的脸。

examples.en: The fair exhibits tools from many countries.
examples.cn: 博览会展出许多国家的工具。

examples.en: Her face exhibited no sign of fear.
examples.cn: 她脸上没有露出恐惧的迹象。

examples.en: The small exhibit drew a large crowd.
examples.cn: 这件小展品吸引了大批观众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ hibit（持有）」——把东西拿到外面举着，就是展出；把情绪摆在脸上，就是表现出。

root: 拉丁语 exhibere（向外呈出）＝ ex-（出）＋ habere（持有）→ exhibit，核心义「拿出去给人看」。

sensesIntro.en: Exhibit means to show something in public, to show a quality or symptom, or an object on display.
sensesIntro.cn: exhibit 意为公开展出、表现出某种特质或症状，或陈列的展品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object in a glass case.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃柜里的一件展品。

branches.en: Public showing is the core sense.
branches.cn: 公开展出是核心义项。

branches.en: Feelings and symptoms are also held out.
branches.cn: 情感与症状同样被展示出来。

branches.en: The noun names the object shown.
branches.cn: 名词指被展示的物品。

branches.en: The act and the object belong together.
branches.cn: 展出行为与展品相互依存。

branches.en: Both senses put something in view.
branches.cn: 两者都把某物放到视野中。

intro.en: Exhibit combines ex-, out, with Latin habere, to hold.
intro.cn: exhibit 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 habere（持有）组成。

latinIntro.en: Exhibere gives exhibitio and then English exhibit.
latinIntro.cn: exhibere 给出 exhibitio，再到英语 exhibit。

items.exampleCN: ex- 标记向外持有。
habere 给出 habit。
exhibere 是直接来源。
exhibit 保留举出展示的意象。
exhibition 指展览。
exhibition 加上了名词词尾。
-or 标记展出者。
exhibitor 加上了表示人的词尾。

latinEntries.example: Exhibere is the source of exhibit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exhibere 是 exhibit 的来源。

definition_zh: 展览会；展览；展示；表现
definition_en: a public show of objects, the act of showing a skill, or a display of feeling
core_image: 挂满画作的长廊
scene: 美术馆正在举办一场现代艺术展。The gallery is holding an exhibition of modern art.
sceneCN: 这里 exhibition 是「展览会」（第 1 个义项）；句意：美术馆正在举办一场现代艺术展。

senses.title: Public show
senses.definition: a public event where objects such as art are shown
senses.definitionCN: 公开展示艺术品等物件的活动
senses.example: The city hosts an annual photo exhibition.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市每年举办一次摄影展。
senses.why: Many objects are held out together for visitors.
senses.whyCN: 许多物件被一起举出供参观者观看。

senses.title: Show of skill
senses.definition: an act of showing a skill or ability to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人展示技能或能力的举动
senses.example: The match was a fine exhibition of passing.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛是一次漂亮的传球展示。
senses.why: Ability is put on display like an object in a hall.
senses.whyCN: 能力像大厅里的展品一样被陈列出来。

senses.title: Display of feeling
senses.definition: a clear show of an emotion or quality
senses.definitionCN: 对某种情绪或特质的明显表露
senses.example: His tears were an exhibition of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 他的眼泪是悲痛的流露。
senses.why: An inner feeling is held out where others can see it.
senses.whyCN: 内心感受被展示出来让人看见。

intro.en: Exhibition comes from Latin exhibitio, a holding out.
intro.cn: exhibition 源自拉丁语 exhibitio，意为向外呈出。

items.en: Habere means to hold.
items.cn: habere 意为持有。

items.en: Exhibere means to hold out or present.
items.cn: exhibere 意为举出、呈出。

items.en: Exhibitio names the act of presenting.
items.cn: exhibitio 指呈出这一行为。

items.en: Old French exhibition keeps the public show sense.
items.cn: 古法语 exhibition 保留公开展示之意。

items.en: English exhibition extends to shows of skill and feeling.
items.cn: 英语 exhibition 扩展到技能与情感的展示。

note.en: An exhibition is the event; an exhibit is one object.
note.cn: exhibition 指整场展览，exhibit 指其中一件展品。

normalIntro.en: An exhibition holds many objects out for the public.
normalIntro.cn: exhibition 把许多物件举出给公众看。

normal.en: The art exhibition opens on Friday.
normal.cn: 艺术展周五开幕。

normal.en: They hold an exhibition every autumn.
normal.cn: 他们每年秋天举办展览。

normal.en: The exhibition hall was full of visitors.

normal.en: Her paintings are on exhibition downtown.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exhibit（展出）＋ ion」——许多东西被摆出来给人看，就是展览会；把本领或情绪摆出来，就是展示与表露。

sensesIntro.en: Exhibition means a public show of objects, a display of skill, or a show of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: exhibition 意为公开展览、技能展示，或情感的表露。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long hall hung with paintings.

branches.en: The public show of objects is the main sense.
branches.cn: 公开展览物件是主要义项。

branches.en: Skill can be exhibited like art.
branches.cn: 技能可以像艺术品一样被展出。

branches.en: Feelings too are put on display.

branches.en: The show can hold objects or emotions.
branches.cn: 展览既能承载物件，也能承载情绪。

definition_zh: 兴奋；欢欣；振奋；刺激
definition_en: a strong feeling of happiness, energy, and excitement
core_image: 瓶盖刚被拧开，气泡一下子涌到瓶口
scene: 第一次独自骑车冲下长坡，风灌进耳朵，她忍不住喊出声来。She felt pure exhilaration as the bicycle flew down the long slope.
sceneCN: 这里 exhilaration 是「兴奋」（第 1 个义项：喜悦与活力同时涌上来）；句意：自行车飞驰下长坡时，她感到纯粹的兴奋。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，加 -ation 成为名词；义为「使兴奋；使振奋」
动词加 -ed，义为「感到兴奋的」，描述人的状态
动词加 -ing，义为「令人兴奋的」，描述事情或经历
与 hilaris 同源的兄弟词，义为「欢闹；大笑」

senses.title: A lifted feeling of joy and energy
senses.definition: a strong feeling of happiness and energy that seems to lift you up
senses.definitionCN: 一种强烈的喜悦与活力，仿佛把人整个人托起来
senses.example: A wave of exhilaration swept over the crowd when the band appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队出现时，一阵兴奋扫过人群。
senses.why: Latin hilaris means cheerful, so the noun names the mood of being made cheerful, not just any pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 hilaris 意为愉快的，所以这个名词指的是「被弄得高兴起来」的那种心境，而不只是普通的快乐。

senses.title: Something that produces the high
senses.definition: an experience or thing that produces this lifted feeling, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 能制造这种高昂感受的经历或事物，常用复数
senses.example: The exhilarations of a first year abroad are hard to describe.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外第一年的种种兴奋很难描述。
senses.why: Once a feeling is well known, the word can be turned around to name the cause, and the plural collects several such causes.
senses.whyCN: 一种感受被人熟悉之后，词就可以反过来指造成它的东西，而复数则把好几件这样的事收在一起。

senses.title: The bodily rush behind the mood
senses.definition: the physical side of the feeling, a rush of energy in the body after effort, danger, or a shock
senses.definitionCN: 这种感受在身体上的一面：用力、涉险或受惊之后体内涌起的一股劲
senses.example: Runners often speak of the exhilaration that comes after the hardest mile.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者常说起最艰难的那一英里之后涌上来的那种欣快。
senses.why: Because the root word describes a whole state of being cheered, it covers the body as well as the mood, which is why sport and danger produce it.
senses.whyCN: 因为词根描述的是一整个「被振奋起来」的状态，它既管情绪也管身体，所以运动与冒险最容易把它激出来。

senses.title: A restorative lift in old medicine
senses.definition: in older medical writing, the act of restoring strength and good spirits to a patient
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的医学文献中，指让病人恢复体力与精神的举动
senses.example: The old treatise lists wine among the means of exhilaration.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧医书把葡萄酒列为提神的手段之一。
senses.why: Early doctors used the verb for making a patient cheerful and strong again, so the noun once belonged to treatment rather than to thrill.
senses.whyCN: 早期医生用这个动词表示让病人重新高兴、重新有力，所以这个名词一度属于治疗，而不是属于刺激。

intro.en: Exhilaration comes from Latin exhilarare, to make cheerful, built on hilaris, cheerful, which is generally taken from Greek hilaros.
intro.cn: exhilaration 来自拉丁语 exhilarare（使高兴），其底子是 hilaris（愉快的），一般认为借自希腊语 hilaros。

items.en: Hilaros means cheerful, merry, or in good spirits.
items.cn: hilaros 意为愉快的、欢畅的、心情好的。

items.en: Latin borrows the adjective as hilaris, cheerful.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借过去，写作 hilaris，意为愉快的。

items.en: The prefix ex- plus hilaris gives exhilarare, to make someone cheerful.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加 hilaris 构成 exhilarare，意为使某人高兴起来。

items.en: Exhilaratio names the state of being cheered, and passes into learned use.
items.cn: exhilaratio 指「被振奋起来」的状态，并进入学术用语。

items.en: English takes the word as exhilaration, first for the condition of being cheered.
items.cn: 英语以 exhilaration 的形式借入，最初指被振奋的状态。

items.en: The meaning narrows toward high spirits, physical thrill, and the lift that speed or danger gives.
items.cn: 词义收窄到高昂的情绪、身体的刺激，以及速度或危险带来的那股振奋。

note.en: Exhilaration belongs with exhilarate, exhilarating, hilarity, and hilarious, and stands near the words for intense joy.
note.cn: exhilaration 与 exhilarate、exhilarating、hilarity、hilarious 同族，并与表示强烈喜悦的词相邻。

entries.definition: to make someone feel happy and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到高兴而充满活力

entries.definition: exciting and full of energy
loud and cheerful laughter
a very strong feeling of happiness and well being
a feeling of great happiness and pride
a sudden strong feeling of excitement

normalIntro.en: Hold on to the fizzing bottle: exhilaration is the pressure of good spirits rising inside a person.
normalIntro.cn: 记住那只冒泡的瓶子：exhilaration 就是好心情在人体内往上顶的那股压力。

normal.en: A surge of exhilaration ran through the team after the winning goal.
normal.cn: 制胜球之后，一阵兴奋传遍全队。

normal.en: Sheer exhilaration kept her awake long after the climb.
normal.cn: 纯粹的兴奋让她在攀登结束后很久都睡不着。

normal.en: The exhilaration of speed is the whole point of the sport.
normal.cn: 速度带来的刺激正是这项运动的意义所在。

normal.en: Compare exhilarating and exhilarated: a fast ride is exhilarating, the passenger is exhilarated.
normal.cn: 对比 exhilarating 与 exhilarated：飞驰的车程令人兴奋，车上的人则感到兴奋。

normal.en: Hilarity and hilarious share the cheerful root, but they name laughter rather than the lifted mood.
normal.cn: hilarity 与 hilarious 共享「愉快」词根，但它们指笑声，而不是那种被托起来的情绪。

abstract.en: Picture a bottle of soda just opened, fizz climbing to the rim and spilling over.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶汽水刚被拧开，气泡一路涌到瓶口溢出来。

abstract.en: Imagine the front car of a roller coaster tipping over the crest, your stomach left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象过山车的第一节车厢翻过最高点，你的胃还留在后面。

abstract.en: Think of stepping into cold sea water on a hot day, the shock turning into a tingle across the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象热天走进冰凉的海水，那一激变成遍布全身的酥麻。

examples.en: The exhilaration of the first solo flight stayed with her for days.
examples.cn: 第一次独自飞行带来的兴奋在她心里停留了好几天。

examples.en: He could not hide his exhilaration when the results were announced.
examples.cn: 结果公布时，他藏不住自己的兴奋。

examples.en: There is a strange exhilaration in walking through a storm.
examples.cn: 在暴风雨中行走，会有一种奇特的兴奋。

dict_mnemonic.text: exhilaration 读快了像中文的「一个劲乐」：高兴得一个劲地乐；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、加强）+ hilaris（愉快的，一般认为借自希腊语 hilaros）→ exhilarare（使高兴）→ 晚期拉丁语 exhilaratio → 英语 exhilaration，核心义「心里的高兴被激出来、往外冒」。

sensesIntro.en: A cheerful root first gives the lifted mood, then the thing that causes it, then the same lift felt in the body, and finally an older sense of being restored by treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 「愉快」这个词根先给出被托起来的情绪，再给出造成它的事物，接着是身体上的同一股上扬，最后是旧时医学里「被调养得恢复精神」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bottle uncapped, the fizz rushing to the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：瓶盖一开，气泡直冲瓶口。

branches.en: The lifted mood is the plain sense people use every day.
branches.cn: 被托起来的情绪，是人们日常使用的那一层。

branches.en: A cause of that mood can be counted, which gives the plural use.
branches.cn: 造成这种情绪的事物可以被数出来，于是有了复数用法。

branches.en: The same lift shows up in the body during sport or danger.
branches.cn: 同一股上扬在运动或冒险时显现在身体上。

branches.en: Early medicine used the word for a patient being cheered back to strength.
branches.cn: 早期医学用这个词指病人被调养得重新高兴、重新有力。

branches.en: Mood and body are two readings of one event, which is why a hard climb can leave you both happy and shaking.
branches.cn: 情绪与身体是同一件事的两种读法，所以一次艰苦的攀登会让人又高兴又发抖。

intro.en: Exhilaration is ex- plus hilaris plus -ation: a prefix of outward movement, an adjective meaning cheerful, and a noun ending for a state.
intro.cn: exhilaration 由 ex- 加 hilaris 加 -ation 构成：一个表示向外的前缀、一个意为愉快的形容词、一个表状态的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin hilaris, cheerful, is generally derived from Greek hilaros, and with ex- it becomes the verb exhilarare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hilaris（愉快的）一般认为源自希腊语 hilaros，加上 ex- 就成为动词 exhilarare。

items.example: The prefix ex- pushes the cheer outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把这份高兴往外推。

items.example: Hilaros is the older Greek shape behind the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: hilaros 是拉丁词背后更早的希腊语形态。

items.example: Hilaris gives the family its cheerful core.
items.exampleCN: hilaris 给这个词族提供了「愉快」的核心。

items.example: Exhilarare joins the prefix to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: exhilarare 把前缀与形容词合在一起。

items.example: Exhilaratio turns the action into a state that can be named.
items.exampleCN: exhilaratio 把这个动作变成可以被命名的状态。

items.meaningCN: 动作或由此形成的状态
items.example: The suffix -ation carries the Latin noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把这个拉丁名词带进英语。

items.example: Exhilarate is the verb that stands behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: exhilarate 是名词背后那个动词。

items.meaning: feeling happy and full of energy
items.example: Exhilarated describes the person who feels the lift.
items.exampleCN: exhilarated 描述那个感到上扬的人。

items.example: Exhilarating describes the ride, not the rider.
items.exampleCN: exhilarating 描述那趟车程，而不是乘客。

items.example: Hilarity keeps the cheerful root without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: hilarity 保留了「愉快」词根，却没有那个前缀。

items.example: Hilarious is the adjective of laughter rather than of thrill.
items.exampleCN: hilarious 属于「大笑」而不是「刺激」那一侧。
